gloss: to state; to assert; to lodge (a complaint, objection)

definitions.gloss: to state; to assert; to lodge (a complaint, objection); to file
definitions.explanation: To formally state or put forward something — an opinion, complaint, objection, or claim — to an authority or in an official setting. Compound of {申|もう}す (humble "to say") + {立|た}てる (to put forward). Used in legal, administrative, and business contexts.

examples.japanese: {異議|いぎ}を{申|もう}し{立|た}てる。
{被告人|ひこくにん}は{無罪|むざい}を{申|もう}し{立|た}てた。
{判決|はんけつ}に{不服|ふふく}があれば、{二週間以内|にしゅうかんいない}に{控訴|こうそ}を{申|もう}し{立|た}てる{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: If you are dissatisfied with the judgment, you need to lodge an appeal within two weeks.

notes:
Compound of {申|もう}す (humble form of "to say") + {立|た}てる ("to set up, put forward"). The verb has a formal, often legal or administrative tone — not used for casual statements.

TRANSITIVITY: Transitive. The thing being asserted takes を: {意見|いけん}を{申|もう}し{立|た}てる.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {異議|いぎ}を{申|もう}し{立|た}てる: to raise an objection
- {不服|ふふく}を{申|もう}し{立|た}てる: to file a complaint of dissatisfaction
- {無罪|むざい}を{申|もう}し{立|た}てる: to plead not guilty
- {権利|けんり}を{申|もう}し{立|た}てる: to assert a right
- {控訴|こうそ}を{申|もう}し{立|た}てる: to lodge an appeal

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {主張|しゅちょう}する: to assert; to claim — broader, everyday register
- {申|もう}し{出|で}る: to come forward to say; to offer/propose — more for volunteering information or requests; less adversarial
